scope: Footer effective context and output rate; custom OpenAI-compatible provider; per-connection insecure TLS; provider form review

tls.server: loopback httptest HTTPS with self-signed certificate
tls.catalog: rejected by default; accepted only for opted-in profile; rejected again after disabling
tls.inference: same opt-in isolation verified for chat completion and streaming
tls.origin_isolation: cross-origin request blocked before target handler
tls.ui: compatible preset, unique connection ID, persisted flag, default off, warning and geometry at 60x20 verified
limitations: No external custom gateway or user credentials used
Native Ollama TLS override is unsupported; opt-in applies to compatible APIs only

footer.effective_context: uses cached effective request window; configured/catalog capacity is initial fallback
footer.token_counts: provider usage or marked estimate; previous measurement is not relabeled as current
footer.rate: provider generation duration when supplied; otherwise marked client-observed request duration
footer.isolation: rate scoped to session and selected model; no previous result presented as live while busy
footer.geometry: single row; width and click coordinates verified from 36 to 180 columns

coverage: real factual project response and evidence flow
effective /16k context and non-empty tok/s in footer
one exact bash approval; no replay
live terminal output before process exit

development_findings: Configurable agent proxy needed to forward UsageControl for footer metrics to work in the shipped application
Mouse assertion used byte offsets; corrected it to terminal cell widths
New page test required explicit offline configuration initialization
First final suite attempt hit temporary-directory disk quota; repeated successfully with workspace cache and temporary directory
limits: Output speed is the last completed model call, not instantaneous streaming telemetry
UI review is code/test based, not a user study or accessibility certification
Broader model-quality comparison was not rerun because prompts, citation gates and evaluation criteria were unchanged
